text: Environmental engineer and data scientist working in the global water, sanitation and health (WASH) sector. Open Science Specialist at ETH Zurich. I develop data science training, build open-data communities, and provide consulting to help manage the world's sanitation challenges. My work spans every sector under the sun, which has made me highly adaptable and empathetic.
I build and maintain open-data communities and FAIR data tooling.
I am passionate about teaching reproducible data science to newcomers.
Wrote and managed a portfolio of ETH Board Open Research Data grants worth roughly CHF 500,000 in total (2023-2026).
Featured recording: [Plan for tomorrow today - a model for data stewardship](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zpVo_-Ne91c) (ETH Library 17:15 Kolloquium).

My research sits at the intersection of environmental engineering, global sanitation, and data science. I work on methods to quantify and characterise faecal sludge, city-wide sanitation monitoring, and the tools and open data that make this work reproducible.
I build and lead open-data communities and FAIR data tooling for the water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) sector, and I write and manage the grants that fund them.
I teach reproducible data science with R and Quarto to newcomers, from graduate courses to free online cohorts and hands-on workshops for scientists and civil servants.
Selected coverage, recordings and video features of my work on open research data and sanitation.
Occasional writing on data stewardship, open science and reproducible research, mostly on the Global Health Engineering blog.
